added.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

As Head of Regulated Industries – Customer Success at Anthropic, you'll lead the Success teams responsible for our most complex Financial Services (FSI) and Healthcare & Life Sciences (HCLS) customers. Think banks, insurers, asset and wealth managers and financial data providers; health systems, hospitals and payers; and pharmaceutical, biotech and life-sciences organizations. You'll directly coach and develop a team of Customer Success Managers who drive value across the full product portfolio (Claude Platform, Claude Code, Claude Cowork). These are organizations where deployment runs through compliance, procurement, security review, model risk and legal before it reaches an end user.

You'll partner day to day with the Regulated Industries sales organization so that customers experience one Anthropic from first conversation to production. You'll turn what works at one regulated customer into a methodology that works at the next. That means success plans that anticipate the governance gates. Executive programs that reach the CIO, CISO, CRO and compliance leaders who decide whether Claude gets deployed. Expansion plays that survive long procurement cycles.

You’ll inherit a partially formed team, spanning individual contributors and managers. You'll hire and run the initial team yourself. As the book expands you'll continue to add managers underneath you and manage through them. We're looking for someone who has already led a success business in regulated environments and wants to build the operating model that lets it scale.

Responsibilities

Directly manage and develop a team of Customer Success Managers covering Financial Services and Healthcare & Life Sciences enterprise accounts — the Regulated Industries book — across all Anthropic products.
Own the hiring plan for the team, including sourcing for regulated-industry experience, onboarding and ramp design; later, hire and develop team leads and shift to managing through them.
Coach the team on success practice specific to regulated customers. That includes navigating compliance, procurement, security and model-risk reviews; building champions across business, technology and risk functions; change management under strict controls; and value realization across consumption and seat-based models.
Drive team accountability to core CS metrics: expansion (consumption growth, adoption), customer health, retention (NRR) and customer satisfaction (CSAT).
Join strategic customer engagements and escalations, with executive presence in front of CIOs, CISOs, chief risk and compliance officers, heads of business lines and board-level sponsors.
Build and refine the regulated-industries success methodology. Success planning frameworks that map the governance path to consumption; QBR and executive-briefing templates; security and compliance readiness playbooks; reference architectures and expansion playbooks that transfer from one regulated customer to the next.
Partner closely with the Regulated Industries sales organization to align on account strategy, set clear ownership between AEs and CSMs, and manage handoffs so long deployment cycles don't stall between teams.
Collaborate with Product, Engineering, Security, Legal and Marketing to advocate for regulated customers' needs and translate field signal into product direction.
Establish an AI-first, innovation-focused team culture; improve team processes and deepen hands-on product expertise.
Conduct regular 1:1s, performance reviews and career development planning for direct reports.
Own portfolio-level planning and forecasting, including renewal-risk mitigation and consumption development across the regulated book.
Serve as the escalation point for at-risk customers and complex situations in the team's portfolio.
Develop advocacy assets for regulated customers: case studies, references and reference architectures that can be shared within compliance constraints.
Champion responsible AI deployment practices with customers and represent Anthropic's values in every customer interaction.

You May Be a Good Fit If You Have

10+ years in customer success, account management or customer-facing roles, with 5+ years of front-line management experience; 2+ years of experience managing managers.
Direct experience driving a Success business with regulated customers — financial services, healthcare and life sciences, or comparable regulated sectors. That means working through compliance, procurement, security review, risk and legal gates and consensus-building across executives to get to consumption.
A proven track record of managing and building customer success teams in SaaS, API or AI/ML companies.
Experience managing enterprise portfolios, including accounts with multi-million dollar annual contract values and deployment cycles measured in quarters, not weeks.
Demonstrated ability to drive outcomes in organizations with many decision-makers and no single owner, and to coach a team to do the same.
A strong understanding of both consumption-based and seat-based business models, with a record of driving adoption, expansion and value realization across them.
Experience developing repeatable frameworks, playbooks or enablement programs that other teams adopted independently of you.
Technical fluency to understand AI/ML products and the deployment, data and security considerations regulated customers raise.
Working knowledge of the regulatory and compliance frameworks these customers operate under e.g. HIPAA, FDA and healthcare data-security requirements
Strong executive presence with both business and risk-side leaders. Represents Anthropic credibly in a CISO or model-risk conversation as well as a CFO one.
Strong business acumen: articulating value, calculating ROI and driving customer business outcomes.
The ability to balance strategic thinking with tactical execution, and to context-switch between coaching, customer engagement and operational planning.
A knack for bringing order to chaos and an enthusiastic "roll up your sleeves" mentality
Passion for responsible AI development and for helping customers transform their businesses with cutting-edge technology.

We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

added.title: Senior Director of Product Marketing
added.description:
About Veriff

Veriff guarantees trust for some of the largest consumer platforms in the world. We're known for identity verification, but that is only where we started. Every verification we run strengthens the Veriff Network, a trust layer that gets smarter with each check. On top of it, we're building a portfolio of products that help platforms know who, and what, they're dealing with at global scale.

The market hasn't caught up with that story yet. We need someone to change that.

The role

You'll lead product marketing at Veriff, and your first mandate is to reposition the company. Today we're seen mainly as an identity verification vendor. We need the market to see the truth: That Veriff is a trust platform behind the world's largest consumer brands. You'll own positioning, messaging, launches, and sales enablement across our portfolio.

This is a hands-on role. You'll write much of the work yourself, including positioning docs, launch plans, pitch narratives, and battlecards, working closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, and Marketing. You'll start with a small team and grow it as our rebuilt sales organization gains traction.

We're looking for someone who will push us. If you have a strong point of view, like to take smart risks, and would rather make a leadership team a little uncomfortable than blend into the category, keep reading.

What You'll Do

Lead Veriff's repositioning. Define how the company, the Veriff Network, and our portfolio are positioned, and get the leadership team, sales team, and market behind it.
Run product launches end to end, making each one strengthen the company story. Work within a structured annual launch cadence and industry event calendar.
Equip our sales team to win enterprise deals with pitch narratives, discovery guides, battlecards, and objection handling. Stay close enough to deals to know what's working, and fix what isn't.
Build competitive and market intelligence, and turn win/loss insight into sharper positioning and better product strategy.
Partner with Product on pricing, packaging, and roadmap narrative, and with Marketing and Communications on campaigns and external storytelling.
Develop our PMM team, and shape when and how it grows.

What We're Looking For

8+ years in product marketing, including time leading the function or a significant part of it, ideally in technical B2B businesses such as AI, SaaS, identity, fraud, payments, security, or API-first companies.
A strong point of view, and a track record of acting on it. You've pushed a differentiated positioning through real internal resistance, and you can show what it achieved.
Bold but honest. In a business where trust is the product, you make ambitious claims you can prove.
Craft. You've personally written positioning for technical products that works for technical and business buyers alike, and you can make a complex trust topic land in one slide.
Proven impact on sales outcomes. You've built enablement that measurably moved conversion, win rates, or deal velocity.
Technical curiosity. You enjoy understanding how sophisticated AI products actually work, so you can explain them in a way nobody else can.
A bias for action. You'd rather write the first draft than wait for direction, and you also enjoy developing the people around you.

Nice to have

Familiarity with regulated industries (financial services, gaming, marketplaces) or developer-led go-to-market motions.

Why Veriff?

We are the preferred identity verification platform partner for the world’s most innovative growth-driven organizations helping conveniently verify and safeguard users anywhere in the world. We support the broadest number of identity documents from nearly every country and territory in the world - and this is continually increasing! With a diverse team in the United States, United Kingdom, Spain, Brazil, and Estonia, as well as robust backing and funding from investors including Accel, Alkeon, IVP, Tiger Capital, and Y Combinator, we’re dedicated to helping businesses and individuals build a safer and more secure world. We strive to be the benchmark for trust online, and we take pride in being a positive force.

Compensation

The base salary for this role is $200,000 - $220,000 per year. Please note that our salary ranges are based on current market data and the offered compensation may vary based on experience, skills, location, and other factors permitted by law

When you join Team Veriff, we offer you the opportunity to have a real impact and advance your career, while looking after you along the way with a range of benefits designed with you in mind. Some of our favorites include…

Flexibility to work from home
Stock options that ensure your share in our success
Extra recharge days on top of your annual vacation
Extensive medical, dental, and vision insurance to ensure you’re feeling great physically and mentally
Learning and Development and Health and Sports budget that you are free to tailor to your own needs
Four weeks of fully paid sabbatical leave after reaching your 5th work anniversary

We are an Equal Opportunities employer committed to a diverse and representative team. Different opinions, perspectives and personalities push us forward. We want to hear from people who are passionate about their work and align with our values. Regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability. We also know the confidence gap and imposter syndrome can get in the way of meeting spectacular candidates - so rest assured, whoever you are, we want to hear from you!

Please take the time to read our Recruitment Privacy Notice, which explains how we collect and process your data for recruitment-related activities in accordance with applicable laws. Please read the information carefully. By submitting the application with the required information, you acknowledge that Veriff processes the information for recruitment purposes. Please be informed that in the final stage of the recruitment process, we may request that you undergo identity verification. For more information, please see Recruitment Privacy Notice.

Full product roadmap for ZGRI: renter's compliance verification flow, insurance product enrollment, and consolidated operator dashboard (HO4 + TLL).
Operational process discovery and automation planning in close partnership with the operations team.
Carrier engagement: working with external renter's insurance carriers to streamline and automate processes where applicable.
GTM partnership: collaborating with ZGRI's GTM lead on ICP definition, commercial positioning, and the scaling strategy.
Metrics co-ownership: defining and tracking success criteria across compliance rates, TLL enrollment velocity, operator adoption, and revenue growth.
Cross-functional stakeholder management spanning operations, sales, engineering, finance, and external carrier partners.

6+ years in product management, with demonstrated 0-to-1 experience building new products or product lines from an early stage.
Proven ability to translate complex operational processes into product requirements, including direct experience conducting process discovery with operations or compliance teams.
Strong cross-functional stakeholder management, with a track record of aligning sales, operations, and engineering around shared outcomes.
Commercial fluency: ability to engage and partner with a GTM counterpart to define ICP, positioning, and revenue strategy.
Excellent written and verbal communication, including with executive stakeholders and external partners.

Background in insurance, insurtech, or a highly regulated fintech environment — familiarity with carrier relationships, compliance requirements, or insurance product mechanics is a meaningful advantage.
Experience in residential real estate or proptech.

About Delinea

Delinea is a pioneer in securing human and machine identities through intelligent, centralized authorization, empowering organizations to seamlessly govern their interactions across the modern enterprise. Leveraging AI-powered intelligence, Delinea’s leading cloud-native Identity Security Platform applies context throughout the entire identity lifecycle – across cloud and traditional infrastructure, data, SaaS applications, and AI. With deployment in weeks, not months, 90% fewer resources to manage than the nearest competitor, and a 99.995% uptime, Delinea delivers robust security and operational efficiency without compromise. Our success is driven by world-class product leadership, outstanding engineers, and strategic investment from TPG. We value diversity, innovation, and a culture of respect and fairness. If you're ready to push boundaries and challenge the status quo in security, we want to hear from you.

Apply today to help us achieve our mission.

Position Summary

Delinea is seeking a Senior Product Manager to own the browser and mobile access experiences of the Delinea Platform, spanning workforce password management (WPM) and the privileged access workflows that sit alongside it. This portfolio is where users meet the Delinea Platform most frequently: in the browser, where credentials are captured and injected and where access to business resources is initiated, and on the phone, where users authenticate, retrieve credentials, and review and approve access requests away from their desks.

You will own two closely related surfaces and are expected to bring coherence across them:

Browser.
The browser extension is the primary daily-use touchpoint for the broader workforce. You will own the Delinea browser extension (DCM), which delivers standard password manager capabilities — credential capture, autofill, secure generation, sharing, and vault access — alongside privileged workflows. This includes cross-browser support and the distinct release, review, and distribution constraints of browser extension stores; the security model of an extension operating in the page context; and the balance between frictionless autofill and rigorous policy enforcement. You will also own browser-based access to business web and SaaS applications, including applications that do not support federation, with policy enforcement, monitoring, and auditability applied to those sessions.

Mobile.
You will own the mobile applications through which users and administrators interact with the platform, including mobile password and credential management, the Delinea authenticator experience supporting multifactor and push-based approval, and mobile platform administration for reviewing, approving, and acting on access requests, alerts, and approvals from an iOS or Android device. Mobile is not a reduced version of the web experience; you will define which workflows genuinely belong on a phone and how to deliver them with the biometric, secure-enclave, push, and offline capabilities the platform affords.

The access paths in this portfolio are the points at which policy is applied, credentials are brokered, and activity is recorded. As the population of identities requesting access to enterprise resources continues to broaden, you will help determine how these capabilities adapt.

This is a high-ownership role in a globally distributed organization. You will operate across Engineering, UX, Architecture, Product Marketing, Support, and Customer Success, and you will engage directly with administrators, security architects, and end users to validate direction. This position is remote and can be based anywhere in the United States.

Key Responsibilities

Own and articulate a multi-year product vision and strategy for Delinea's browser and mobile access experiences across workforce password management and adjacent privileged access use cases, aligned to company objectives and market opportunity.
Translate that strategy into a prioritized roadmap and backlog spanning the DCM browser extension, browser-based application access, and the mobile credential management, authenticator, and platform administration applications — making explicit trade-off decisions with agile development teams.
Drive the browser extension roadmap end to end, including cross-browser parity, extension store submission and review cycles, permission and manifest changes, update and rollback strategy, and the credential capture and autofill experience.
Define the mobile product strategy across iOS and Android, including authenticator flows, biometric and secure-element usage, push-based approval workflows, offline behavior, and app store release management, and determine where and when stronger authentication factors should be introduced.
Ensure a coherent access experience across surfaces: consistent policy enforcement, credential injection, session handling, and audit behavior whether access originates in a browser, an extension, or a mobile device, in coordination with the owners of adjacent access clients.
Establish a durable point of view on the market by engaging directly with customers, partners, analysts, and internal stakeholders; validate requirements through structured discovery rather than anecdote.
Partner with Engineering, UX, QA, and Support to deliver high-quality, performant experiences across supported browsers and mobile operating systems.
Balance sustaining investment in established capabilities against the platform migration path and new zero-to-one work; build the business case for where to invest.
Anticipate how access patterns and enforcement requirements evolve over the roadmap horizon, and sequence investment so the portfolio remains extensible as those requirements change.
Define adoption, engagement, and success metrics for each surface, and use them to inform prioritization and demonstrate business value.
Shape go-to-market strategy with Product Marketing, driving positioning, messaging, packaging, and pricing across the workforce password management and privileged access buying centers, which frequently differ.
Enable Sales, Support, and Customer Success with the context, collateral, and training needed for launches and ongoing customer success.
Stay current on browser security, credential and secrets management, application access, and passwordless and FIDO2 authentication trends to inform roadmap evolution.

Skills & Requirements

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Business, or a related field preferred; Master's or MBA a plus.
6+ years of product management experience in an Agile/Scrum environment, including end-to-end ownership of an enterprise product line.
5+ years in software, SaaS, or cloud security, with direct exposure to password management, authentication, privileged access management, or client-side access technologies.
Demonstrated experience shipping and operating browser extensions, mobile applications, or both at enterprise scale, including familiarity with the release, review, distribution, and versioning constraints of extension and app stores.
Working knowledge of browser security fundamentals relevant to extension development: content scripts and page-context isolation, extension permission models and manifest versioning, same-origin policy, and secure credential handling in the browser.
Working knowledge of mobile platform capabilities relevant to identity: biometric authentication, secure enclave and keystore, push notification services, mobile device and application management, and platform privacy requirements.
Familiarity with identity and authentication standards: OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SAML, SCIM, FIDO2/WebAuthn, TOTP, and mTLS.
Understanding of browser-delivered application access, including federated and non-federated login flows, credential injection, and the monitoring and audit of application sessions.
Familiarity with machine and non-human identity concepts — secrets management, service accounts, workload identity, and short-lived credentials — is a plus.
Deep familiarity with enterprise endpoint and IT environments: Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android; Active Directory and Entra ID; endpoint and mobile management tooling.
Working knowledge of public cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud Platform) and cloud-native, microservices-based architectures.
Proven track record of taking enterprise products from concept to general availability and growing them into meaningful revenue, translating technical capability into compelling offerings and user experiences.
Strong user-experience instinct. These are high-frequency, daily-use tools; friction in the access path has a direct and measurable cost.
Analytical mindset capable of balancing customer needs, competitive positioning, and business growth opportunities.
Certifications such as Pragmatic Marketing or Scrum Product Owner are advantageous.
Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, including experience presenting to executive leadership, analysts, and enterprise customers — fluent in English.

We're Fundraise Up – a global fundraising platform built to make donating to nonprofits fast, seamless and accessible to all. Our mission is to unlock the world's generosity potential by optimising how people give.

About The Role

Most new bets don't fail. They just never get killed. You'll make sure every one ends in a decision.

Fundraise Up is investing in a Lab to explore new product lines and step-change growth opportunities. The Lab runs like a small startup inside the company, turning ambiguous opportunities into shipped pilots and clear investment decisions. As the Lab's first and only permanent owner, you'll personally drive discovery, experimentation and early delivery with Engineering and Design. You'll make explicit Scale, Iterate, Pivot or Kill calls based on evidence. This is a senior individual contributor role with real authority to pursue high-impact bets, and a clear expectation to kill bad ideas early.

Key Responsibilities

Own the Lab portfolio. Build and run a single, visible, prioritised portfolio. Every bet has a clear hypothesis, expected upside, effort, dependencies, owner and next decision point.
Set a repeatable prioritisation method. Weigh signals, confidence, upside, GTM dependency and effort so bets are chosen on evidence, not enthusiasm.
Design experiments that can fail cleanly. Name the riskiest assumptions for each bet and set explicit kill criteria before you start. Deliver a 4–8 week experiment plan in your first months.
Run fast and ship just enough. Use spikes, prototypes, Wizard of Oz tests and pilots to learn quickly without overbuilding. Instrument every pilot to capture meaningful signals.
Make the call. Turn outcomes into crisp Scale, Iterate, Pivot or Kill decisions, with no zombie projects. Keep lightweight decision logs and learning summaries so leadership and GTM stay aligned.
Secure the team per bet. Engineering and Design support is assigned on demand, so make it explicit for each top-priority initiative and set a working cadence.
Get ahead of GTM. Coordination with GTM is usually the hardest part. Flag dependencies early (positioning, enablement, pricing, legal, support) and drive alignment across teams.
Hand over winners cleanly. When the signal is strong, package what was validated, the evidence, remaining risks, success metrics and a recommended scaling plan.
Work AI-native. At Fundraise Up, AI is a default tool, not an experimental one. We expect every team member to use AI actively in their day-to-day work, spot where AI can change the shape of problems in their function, and grow their fluency as the tools evolve. In the Lab, that means using AI for research, synthesis, prototyping and analysis to move faster, while keeping judgement sharp.

Comfort as the driver, with minimal delegation and maximum ownership
Strong written communication: concise decision logs, learning summaries and alignment artifacts
Practical use of AI as leverage for research, synthesis, prototyping and analysis
Fluent written and spoken English [TO CONFIRM]

Launching early-stage products into market with measurable adoption or revenue signals
Working closely with GTM teams on positioning, enablement and early go-to-market motion

Would rather kill a bet in week three than defend it in month six
Structure your own specs, experiments and execution without waiting for someone else to
Enjoy ambiguity and fast changes of direction more than stable roadmaps and long planning cycles
Value clear thinking over looking busy
Say the uncomfortable thing early, especially to GTM and leadership
Get energy from real customers, real data and real constraints
Ship the smallest thing that answers the question
Want ownership, with the authority to match

It’s hard to believe that it’s 2026 and paying rent on time is expensive, inflexible, and difficult. We’re here to change that! Our mission is to empower as many renters as possible with flexibility over their most significant recurring expense. Will you be a part of the team?

About The Role

As a Principal Product Designer at Flex, you’ll solve problems for consumers across the country who are underserved by existing financial products. We’re handling people’s most significant recurring expense, which means the stakes of getting the experience right are real: a confusing screen or a poorly handled edge case can cost someone a late fee, a credit mark, or a difficult conversation with their leasing office.

We’re looking for a designer to lead a full area of our business. You’ll shape and drive the vision for your vertical, and you’ll be accountable for how it connects to everything around itThe experience only holds together if someone is responsible for the whole of it, not just their team’s slice. That means setting direction, aligning several teams around one coherent picture, and raising the quality bar across all of them.

This is an individual contributor role with the influence of a leader. Your leverage comes from the artifacts you make, the standards you set, and the designers you make better, not from a reporting line. You’ll still be deep in the work leading design exploration on the most critical projects, and building the prototypes that show where a body of work is headed and what it will unlock.

This is a highly measured, highly cross-functional environment, with a big opportunity for designers to bridge true customer needs with creative solutions. You’ll work alongside product managers, engineers, data analysts, risk, and compliance partners, and most of what you design will run as an experiment before it becomes the default. The designers who do their best work here are highly creative with solutioning, curious about the numbers, comfortable with constraints, and willing to change their minds when the evidence says to. All of your design skills will be put to use, from design thinking to interaction design and visual design.

What You’ll Do

Lead design for a full area of the business by shaping and driving the vision for your vertical, and owning the strategy and end-to-end execution that delivers it
Connect and align multiple teams through complex design challenges, weaving separate visions into one cohesive ecosystem
Lead design exploration and solutions on the most critical projects across your area, staying close enough to the work to set the standard by doing it
Consistently set a high bar for quality across features, concepts, and innovative solutions. Hold the bar through the standards you define, the critiques you lead, and the feedback you give designers on any team your area touches
Design for people under real financial pressure by bringing clarity, honesty, and dignity to flows where money and consequences are involved, including the error, pending, and recovery states that are easy to leave for last
Build the prototypes and artifacts that paint a picture of where your body of work is headed, and use them to align partners and leadership on the opportunities worth going after
Play a pivotal role in strategic initiatives by supporting your team and company strategy with a wide range of inputs: qualitative research, data, industry trends, and your own design expertise
Partner with PM, analytics, risk, and engineering to structure experiments. Define hypotheses to test, what a guardrail should protect, and what a result would actually prove
